paper.title_en: Magnetic History and Field Sweep Rate Effects on Transformation Hysteresis in $\mathrm{Ni}_{41}\mathrm{Co}_{9}\mathrm{Mn}_{31.5}\mathrm{Ga}_{18.5}$
paper.abstract_en: Hysteresis in magnetic-field-induced structural phase transformations is a major obstacle to the application of metamagnetic shape memory alloys. One promising approach to reduce hysteresis is to utilize a metastable martensitic state generated by magnetic-field cycling. However, the mechanism by which the metastable state reduces hysteresis remains unclear. Here, microsecond pulsed-field magnetization measurements are used to investigate the transformation kinetics of $\mathrm{Ni}_{41}\mathrm{Co}_{9}\mathrm{Mn}_{31.5}\mathrm{Ga}_{18.5}$. Magnetic-field cycling reduces the hysteresis width by approximately 50-60%, demonstrating that substantial suppression persists on a microsecond timescale. Comparison with millisecond pulsed-field measurements suggests that the reverse martensitic transformation field is more sensitive to the field sweep rate for the metastable martensite than for the initial martensite. Possible explanations include enhanced thermal activation associated with a lower effective activation barrier and differences in the athermal contribution arising from different metastable martensitic microstructures.
